formulation.rationale: Both mapped products are rapid-acting insulin glulisine, with one concentration-unspecified entry and one Apidra U-100 entry. The compared society guidance addresses rapid-acting insulin analogues as a class and does not provide a brand-specific fasting instruction for Apidra U-100.

comparisons.note: The Endocrine Society explicitly distinguishes nutritional/bolus rapid-acting insulin from correction insulin during NPO status and links rapid-acting insulin to meals when patients are eating.
The Austrian Diabetes Association supports monitored perioperative correction with rapid-acting insulin or insulin analogues.

comparisons.checked_locators: Recommendations Before Colonoscopy > Patient Education and Navigation
comparisons.note: USMSTF directs individualized antihyperglycemic medication management with the prescribing clinician and gives no glulisine-specific dose.

scenario_coverage.reason: Endocrine Society guidance explicitly holds bolus insulin after fasting/NPO begins.
Society guidance distinguishes holding routine bolus insulin while NPO from correctional rapid-acting insulin based on glucose monitoring.
Endocrine Society guidance keeps bolus insulin held while NPO and links rapid-acting nutritional insulin to resumed eating.

conflicts.description: The Endocrine Society distinguishes routine bolus insulin, which is held while NPO, from correction insulin that may continue; the Austrian Diabetes Association separately supports monitored perioperative correction with rapid-acting insulin or analogues. These source-specific actions are preserved separately.

open_questions.text: USMSTF does not provide a colonoscopy-specific insulin glulisine dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic management with the prescribing clinician.
The actual correctional glulisine dose depends on glucose and the patient's established correction plan; no patient-specific dose is inferred.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package. Routine prandial/bolus glulisine is separated from correctional rapid-acting insulin while fasting. No Apidra-specific perioperative exception was identified.
